01 / About me

Curiosity is my
favourite design tool.

My journey into design has shaped the way I see the relationship between functionality, structure and visual storytelling. With a background in architecture and a degree in Game Design and User Experience, I enjoy connecting what people need with what a product can become.

My process starts with understanding people, exploring ideas and turning them into thoughtful solutions through prototyping, testing and refining. I believe good design goes beyond aesthetics, it’s about creating experiences that genuinely work for people.

Outside of design, I enjoy travelling, discovering new places and finding inspiration in everyday experiences.

Academic project

GoSolo

Everything a solo traveller needs, in one place.

Project type
UX/UI Design
Platform
Mobile Application
Target audience
Solo Travellers
Role
UX Research, UI Design, Interaction Design
Tools
Figma
Duration
Sep 2025 – Nov 2025

Overview

GoSolo is a travel app concept designed to make solo travel feel safer, easier and more socially accessible. By bringing travel planning, safety features and social connections together in one platform, GoSolo aims to help travellers explore independently with greater confidence and peace of mind.

76%

76% of Gen Z and Millennial travelers plan to embark on solo travel experiences in 2025.

42B

The global solo travel market size was estimated at USD 482.34 billion in 2024.

2nd

Solo travel is the second-most popular category for postlockdown trips, says Cox & Kings.

The problem

Travelling alone isn’t always easy.

While solo travel offers freedom and independence, it can also bring uncertainty and anxiety, especially for those unfamiliar with their destinations.

Planning Anxiety

Too many travel options and unfamiliar destinations can make planning overwhelming, leading to decision fatigue.

Safety Concerns

Travellers worry about personal safety, emergencies and navigating unfamiliar environments without immediate support.

Social Isolation

Travelling alone can sometimes feel lonely, while meeting strangers may feel intimidating or unsafe.

How might we

How might we make solo travel feel safer, calmer and more socially accessible?

Research insights

Fear and risk are not the same thing.

Perceived Fears

Anxiety that exists before anything goes wrong, such as worrying about getting lost, feeling lonely or not having someone to rely on.

Actual Risks

Real situational concerns such as unsafe locations, emergencies and unexpected disruptions.

Travellers want to feel safe and supported while maintaining their independence.

Social connections should feel optional, comfortable and safe.

Curated recommendations can reduce the stress of planning.

The solution

An All-in-One Travel Companion

GoSolo brings everything solo travellers need into one convenient platform, combining travel planning, safety features and social connections. From organising itineraries and discovering activities to staying connected with loved ones and meeting fellow travellers, GoSolo makes every step of the journey easier, safer and more enjoyable.

Travel Safety & Check-ins

Share travel itineraries with trusted contacts, manage location-sharing preferences and receive reminders to confirm safety.

Safety screens — add image

Social Connection

Discover nearby verified travellers and connect through shared interests or group activities, making it easier to meet others without pressure.

Connect screens — add image

Smart Booking & Itinerary Management

Keep travel bookings, accommodation, transportation and activities organised in one convenient location.

Itinerary screens — add image

Curated Solo Itineraries

Explore personalised activity recommendations designed around safety, travel preferences and solo-friendly experiences.

Guide screens — add image

Reflection

Working on GoSolo helped me better understand the emotional challenges behind solo travel and the importance of designing beyond functional requirements. I learned how research insights can shape feature decisions and how balancing safety, independence and social interaction can create a more thoughtful user experience. This project also allowed me to explore how multiple travel needs could be brought together into one cohesive platform.

Academic project

Goodreads

Reimagining the reading experience

Project type
UX/UI Design
Platform
Mobile Application
Target audience
Readers
Role
UX Research, UI Design, Interaction Design
Tools
Figma
Duration
Sep 2024 – Nov 2024

Overview

Goodreads is a social platform that allows readers to discover books, track their reading progress, write reviews and connect with other readers. This project explores how Goodreads could be improved through a refreshed user experience, addressing its cluttered interface, inconsistent navigation and limited discoverability. Through user research and interface redesign, I aimed to create a more intuitive and engaging reading experience.

Research findings

What readers struggled with

01

Cluttered Interface

Users described the interface as outdated, overwhelming and difficult to navigate due to dense text and poorly organised content.

02

Limited Feature Discoverability

Many users were unaware of features such as custom shelves, reading statistics, community groups and author-following pages.

03

Inconsistent Mobile Experience

Some features available on the desktop website, such as community groups and group recommendations, were missing or less accessible on mobile.

04

Book Discovery Challenges

Users often relied on ratings and reviews to decide what to read next, making trustworthy reviews and accessible recommendations especially important.

05

Limited Language Diversity

Users wanted better access to books in different languages and from international authors.

How might we

How might we make Goodreads more intuitive, organised and enjoyable for readers to use?

The redesign

Five changes, before and after

01

Homepage

Reworked the homepage to prioritise updates from followed users. When there are no more updates to display, users are shown suggestions of other readers to follow instead of unrelated book recommendations.

02

Search

Simplified the search experience by allowing users to search for books, authors and other readers directly through one search bar.

03

Book Details & Reviews

Reorganised book information to improve readability, introduced half-star ratings and prioritised reviews from friends before community reviews.

The swipe gesture made additional details difficult to discover, so I replaced it with a familiar info (i) icon to make the action more intuitive and recognisable.

Reviews from friends are now displayed before community reviews, allowing users to see opinions from people they follow more easily.

Added half-star ratings to give readers more flexibility when expressing their opinions about a book.

04

Profile

Made the profile easier to access and reorganised the social sections to clarify followers, following and followed authors.

05

Discover & Community

Consolidated book recommendations into one Discover page and made community groups easier to access through a dedicated tab.

Reflection

This project taught me the importance of understanding users before making design decisions. I learned how to turn research findings into practical design improvements, while balancing the needs of different readers. Moving forward, I would like to further refine the design through usability testing.

All projects

Industry project

Spatia

Build what you learn.

Project type
UX/UI Design
Platform
Web Browser
Target audience
Secondary school students
Role
UX Research, UI Design, Interaction Designer, Project Manager
Client
VThere
Duration
Sep 2026 – Current

Overview

Spatia is my final year project, developed in collaboration with industry partner VThere. It is a browser-based 3D spatial editor that allows students aged 13–17 to create and customise their own virtual History museums. Designed for students with little to no experience in 3D modelling or programming, Spatia aims to make 3D creation more accessible through a simplified, beginner-friendly experience that fits into a regular classroom lesson.

Key features

Four ways students build

01. Object Placement & Manipulation

Build and customise the museum by placing objects from the asset bar. Users can easily move, rotate and scale objects to create their desired layout.

Placement animation — add GIF

02. Adding & Customising Content

Bring museum exhibits to life by adding text, images and videos. Users can customise their content to create more engaging and informative exhibits.

Content animation — add GIF

03. Scene Management

Create multiple scenes and viewpoints to organise different areas of the museum.

Scenes animation — add GIF

04. Trigger-based Interactions

Create simple WHEN → DO interactions that let students make objects and spaces respond to visitor actions without writing code.

Triggers animation — add GIF

What’s next

Spatia is an ongoing final year project developed in collaboration with industry partner VThere. Beyond the student-facing editor, the project also involves designing and developing interfaces for other stakeholders, including administrators and facilitators. I am continuing to refine the overall user experience while working towards the project’s next development milestones.
